title: American Potato Salad
subtitle: Creamy mayonnaise potato salad with mustard and pickle
excerpt: American potato salad is dressed in mayonnaise while the potatoes are still warm so the dressing is absorbed. It includes celery for crunch, boiled eggs, and yellow mustard, with a little pickle for sharpness. It's the definitive BBQ side dish alongside coleslaw.
sourceNotes: American potato salad has been a cookout staple since the 19th century, with the mayonnaise-and-mustard formula codifying as the Midwest and Southern standard throughout the 20th century.

recipe.batchNotes: Makes well for a crowd; keeps in the fridge for three days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to a day ahead. The flavour improves after chilling.

content.text: American potato salad is dressed warm so the mayo is absorbed by the still-hot potato. It gives a different result from French potato salad dressed with vinaigrette, or dressed-cold salads that stay waxy. Yellow American mustard is traditional here and gives a distinctly different flavour from Dijon, milder and more vinegary. The eggs are standard: not optional.

items.prepNote: peeled if preferred, cut into 2 cm chunks
finely chopped (or 3 tbsp sweet pickle relish)
yellow American mustard or mild Dijon

content.text: Cook {{waxy-potato}} in well-salted boiling water for 12 to 15 minutes until completely tender when pierced with a knife. Drain and leave to steam for five minutes.

Whisk {{mayonnaise}}, {{american-mustard}}, {{cider-vinegar}}, {{sea-salt-fine}}, and {{black-pepper}} together in a large bowl. Add the warm (not hot) potatoes and toss to coat. The potatoes absorb the dressing as they cool.

Leave to cool for 15 minutes, then fold in {{eggs}}, {{celery}}, {{white-onion}}, {{gherkins}}, and {{flat-leaf-parsley}}. Taste and adjust seasoning. Refrigerate for at least one hour. Dust with {{paprika-smoked}} before serving if you like.

items.symptom: The potato salad is gluey and starchy
items.cause: Waxy potatoes overcooked and broken down, or floury variety used.
items.fix: Use a really waxy potato (Charlotte, Nadine, or new potatoes). Cook until just tender, not falling apart. The potato should hold its shape when tossed with the dressing.

items.symptom: The dressing is thin and pools at the bottom
items.cause: Potatoes were too hot when dressed, causing the mayo to liquefy.
items.fix: Let the potatoes steam dry for five minutes and cool slightly before adding the dressing. They should be warm, not steaming hot.
Season generously before adding the potatoes. Cold dulls seasoning, so the potato salad needs more salt than you'd use in a warm dish.

items.symptom: The onion flavour is too sharp and raw
items.fix: Soak the finely chopped onion in the cider vinegar for ten minutes before adding. This removes the raw bite while keeping the flavour.

content.text: American potato salad is a standard side at a summer cookout, alongside coleslaw and corn on the cob. Every family has a recipe. The variations are minor: pickle relish or gherkins, paprika on top or not, celery seeds in the dressing or not. The mustard-and-mayo version is the Midwest and Southern standard. The German-American version, dressed with bacon fat and vinegar, is a different dish entirely.
